content:
The exact launch timing of the iPhone Ultra remains unclear, with a new supply chain report indicating that Foxconn is making "final adjustments" to the production process. Previous reports had already indicated that mass production has begun.

Recent reports suggest Apple will unveil the new foldable iPhone at its September event, but initial supply may be limited…

What is certain is that Apple has set extremely high quality standards for the production of its first foldable iPhone. The company waited until its display partner Samsung was able to produce a creaseless internal display before formally moving the project forward.

These extremely strict standards are likely to make this product one of the most challenging new products Apple has ever undertaken, carrying with it the risk of production delays. Beyond that, however, much remains unclear.

Some earlier reports hinted that the iPhone Ultra launch could be significantly delayed, possibly pushed to early next year. Later reports pointed to a potential delay of one to two months. Since then, however, the prevailing view has been that even if this upcoming high-end model is delayed, it would only be a short postponement.

Today's DigiTimes report actually doesn't bring much new information. The headline reads "Apple's first foldable iPhone faces production hurdles," but beyond rehashing previously reported content, the article doesn't mention any new issues. The only specific claim is:

This statement could simply refer to a routine step in the production process, rather than a fault requiring adjustments that could lead to delays.

Therefore, the current expectation remains that it will debut alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, with sales beginning shortly thereafter, though initial supply may be limited.
